newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia not giving any more major pacts to IPPs.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia not giving any more major pacts to IPPs.

text.p: Malaysia does not plan to give any more major power contracts to private power companies known as Independent Power Producers (IPPs), Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday.
"We have stopped giving to the IPPs now because I think it's Tenaga's turn to expand," he told reporters at a function for state-controlled utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
"For now, yes, there will be no major opportunities for IPPs," he said.
Government officials including Mahathir over the past week have urged IPPs to take on more socially responsible roles and to not impose unfairly high prices for power on Tenaga.

Tenaga has complained in the past about having to pay too much for power generated by the country's five IPPs. The utility's payments to IPPs made up about 40 percent of its operating costs last year.
Mahathir noted that a 2,000 MW coal-fired power plant which had been proposed recently will be built by Tenaga, not by an IPP.
Malaysia is also considering asking the IPPs to contribute toward the cost of providing power to rural areas. Tenaga has been bearing the costs of that in the past.
